title: A fragment that names one of §5.1's two keys and not the other is refused locally, by name of the missing one
notes: The rule: a client handed this link MUST refuse an invite whose `k` or `h` is missing or is not a 32-byte value, locally and before it opens a socket, and the refusal names the key it is about (§5.1). This vector pins that refusal and its naming, in both directions of both faults: `k` alone is refused for the missing `h`, and `h` alone for the missing `k`; a `k` whose final character carries non-zero padding bits is refused for `k`, and an `h` too short to be a key for `h`. The subject is handed the link and answers the `join` itself, in its own words, because a refusal with no socket on it has no frame to report in; `expectRefusal` asserts the naming and not the sentence, since §5.1 leaves the sentence to the client. The refused legs are also the evidence that none of them seated anything: a subject left in a session after one would report itself seated for the next `start`. The last leg is the control — the whole fragment, which must join — because the other way to pass a corpus of refusals is to refuse everything, and the refusals above differ only in which key they must name. The failure this prevents is a client that dials with half a fragment, or with a value that is not a key: it is seated, receives sealed frames it can neither read nor verify, and publishes frames no conforming peer can attribute, so the room it joins is one it can take no part in.
